statement: In acute $\triangle ABC$ with $\angle B>\angle C$, $M$ is the midpoint of $BC$, $D$ and $E$ are feet of altitudes from $C$ and $B$. $K$ and $L$ are midpoints of $ME$ and $MD$. If $KL$ meets the line through $A$ parallel to $BC$ at $T$, prove $TA=TM$.
Find all naturals $n>2$ for which there exist $n$ naturals $a_1,\ldots,a_n$, not all equal, such that $a_1a_2, a_2a_3, \ldots, a_na_1$ is an arithmetic progression with nonzero common difference.

There are $n>1$ points on a circle. An interval is an arc between consecutive chosen points. Consider a family $F$ of intervals such that each element has at most one other element as a superset. Let $m$ be the number of maximal elements and $a$ the number of non-maximal elements. Prove $n \geq m + a/2$.
A finite set $A$ is good if: (a) $\gcd(a,b,c)=1$ for any three distinct elements; (b) for any two distinct $b,c\in A$ there exists $a\in A$ (distinct from $b,c$) with $a\mid bc$. Find all good sets.
Find all surjective $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ such that for all $x,y$: $f(x+f(x)+2f(y)) = f(2x)+f(2y)$.

From $T$ outside circle $\omega$ (center $O$), draw tangents $TB$ and $TC$. $K$ on $TB$, $H$ on $TC$. (a) $B', C'$ are antipodes of $B, C$ on $\omega$. $K'$ on bisector of $\angle BCO$ with $KK'\perp BC$, $H'$ on bisector of $\angle CBO$ with $HH'\perp BC$. Prove $K,H',B'$ collinear $\Leftrightarrow$ $H,K',C'$ collinear. (b) Two circles inside $TBC$ tangent to each other at $J$ and to $\omega$, with one tangent to $TB$ at $K$ and the other to $TC$ at $H$. Prove $BKJI$ and $CHJI$ are cyclic ($I$ is incenter of $\triangle OBC$).
Find the locus of points $P$ inside equilateral $\triangle ABC$ such that $\sqrt{d(P,\ell_1)} = \sqrt{d(P,\ell_2)} + \sqrt{d(P,\ell_3)}$ for some labeling of the sides.

Let $p$ be prime and $k\leq p$ a positive integer. $f(x)\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$ satisfies $p^k\mid f(x)$ for all $x\in\mathbb{Z}$. (a) Prove there exist $A_0,\ldots,A_k\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$ with $f(x)=\sum_{i=0}^k(x^p-x)^i p^{k-i}A_i(x)$. (b) Give a counterexample for each prime $p$ and $k>p$.

We have $n$ non-collinear points. A line $\ell$ is good if the points can be split into two sets $A$, $B$ with equal sums of distances to $\ell$. Prove there exist infinitely many points through each of which at least $n+1$ good lines pass.

Find the least $k$ such that for all $a,b,c,d\in\mathbb{R}$: $\sqrt{(a^2+1)(b^2+1)(c^2+1)}+\sqrt{(b^2+1)(c^2+1)(d^2+1)}+\sqrt{(c^2+1)(d^2+1)(a^2+1)}+\sqrt{(d^2+1)(a^2+1)(b^2+1)} \geq 2(ab+bc+cd+da+ac+bd)-k$.
Let $\triangle ABC$ with $A', B', C'$ the midpoints of $BC$, $CA$, $AB$. Points $P$ and $P'$ satisfy $PA=P'A'$, $PB=P'B'$, $PC=P'C'$. Prove all lines $PP'$ pass through a fixed point.
$f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ is such that $af(a)+bf(b)+2ab$ is always a perfect square. Prove $f(a)=a$ for all $a$.
